Calley · UI redesign · brief for design partners

The calendar, as it stands

Every significant surface of Calley, photographed from the running application against a real database — followed by the design system underneath it, the five things that are wrong with it, and what we want back.

01Product

What Calley is

A calendar that holds events and tasks in one place, with RFC 5545 recurrence. Single user. No sharing, no invitees, no attachments — a personal planning surface, not a collaboration tool.

Four views, a right-hand task panel, a left sidebar carrying a mini-calendar and the list of calendars, and a settings area. Everything is created and edited through right-hand drawers and modal dialogs; there are no full-page forms inside the app.

The intent expressed in the code is a warm, editorial, paper-like calendar — serif display type on a bone ground, one terracotta accent spent only on actions and on “now”, hairline rules instead of boxes, and a monospace face for figures. On desktop it largely delivers that.

02Foundations

The system underneath

Every token lives in one file — apps/web/src/styles/globals.css. There is no Tailwind config; v4 reads the @theme block directly. Change a token and every component follows.

Core palette

Paper#f8f7f4--color-bg
Card#ffffff--color-surface
Ink#1a1916--color-text
Graphite#716c68--color-text-muted
Ember#bd4c26--color-accent
Rule#e4e2dd--color-border
Edge#918b84--color-border-strong

Status colours sit alongside: forest #3a6b5c for success and low-priority tasks, #c0392b for destructive actions and errors, gold #d4a017 for medium priority. Tints are derived once via color-mix() rather than reinvented per component, and the modal scrim is mixed from Ink rather than black so dimmed content stays warm.

Typography

DisplayDM Serif Display Wordmark, date title, page titles
BodyOutfit 300–700 Everything else · 1.55 line-height
NumericDM Mono 400/500 Times, dates, counts — applied through a .numeric utility with tabular figures

A fluid scale of six steps, ratio ≈1.2, clamped tightly around the sizes already shipping. Line-heights are not tokenised — the repo's stylelint config rejects the --text-*--line-height form, so they fall back to Tailwind defaults.

Shape, depth, motion

Radii 4px pills and tabs · 8px default · 16px dialogs
Shadows Three steps, 6% / 10% / 14% black — cards, popovers, dialogs
Z-index A fixed six-step scale, 100 → 600, not ad-hoc numbers
Motion 120–200ms, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), colour and transform only
Focus One 2px accent outline, defined once at zero specificity
Targets 44px minimum, but only under @media (any-pointer: coarse)

Fixed dimensions a redesign inherits

Topbar 60px
Sidebar 240px open · 60px collapsed · 0 below lg
Task panel 300px at lg+ · 360px at sm · full-width to 400px below
Drawers Right sheet, capped at 512px
Time grid 48px per half hour — 96px/hour, 2304px for a full day
Breakpoints Only three in use. lg (1024px) is the real desktop/mobile boundary
03Editing

Creating and editing

All of it happens in right-hand sheets and stacked dialogs. Nothing navigates away from the calendar.

04Findings

Five things that are wrong

These are the reasons this project exists. Each one is visible in the plates.

Finding one · colour

Three unrelated palettes ship at the same time

A person choosing a calendar colour and a person choosing an event colour are picking from two different sets, neither of which is the product's own palette.

1 — The core system

Warm, editorial, deliberate. Defined in globals.css.

2 — Calendar categories

Twelve flat-UI-era hues in packages/shared/src/constants/colors.ts, only loosely related to the core palette. Plate 31.

3 — Per-event colour override

Eight stock Tailwind defaults, hard-coded in EventDrawer.tsx:104. They belong to no system at all, and they are the loudest thing on any screen they appear on. Plate 18b.

We want one categorical palette, derived from the core system — roughly twelve separable hues that each work as a tint behind Ink text and as a solid 3px rule, with AA-passing text on the tint.

Finding two · mobile

On a phone, the primary actions cannot be reached

Below 1024px the app degrades badly, and it compounds. The sidebar's open state is stored without regard to viewport, so a phone user lands on a drawer and a dimming backdrop laid over their calendar, and has to dismiss it before doing anything at all.

Behind it, the topbar overflows. The centred date navigator and view switcher push search, the primary New button, the task-panel toggle and the account menu past the right edge — not merely cramped, but unreachable.

There is currently no way to create an event, search, open tasks, or sign out from a phone.

Month and Week compound it again: both tabs are hidden below lg, yet the default view is Month — so the first thing a phone user sees is a horizontally clipped month grid they have no control to leave except by choosing Day or Agenda. This is the single largest opportunity in the project.

Finding three · architecture

Settings renders inside the calendar chrome

Every settings page sits beneath a topbar still showing the month title, the Month/Week/Day/Agenda switcher and the Today button — none of which do anything there — with the calendar sidebar still holding 240px on the left. Settings needs its own frame, or the chrome needs to become context-aware.

Finding four · density

Density is uneven in both directions

Month cells show three pills before collapsing to “+N more” — and “+N more” is not an expander. It navigates to that date's Day view, dropping the month context entirely. Meanwhile the time grid runs at a generous 96px/hour, and Agenda renders a full-height “No events or tasks” row for every empty day, so a quiet week costs several screens of scrolling.

Finding five · empty states

The empty states are written, tested, and never shown

An EmptyState component ships with three product-specific presets — “Nothing scheduled”, “No tasks here”, “No results for…” — each with an icon, a calm line of copy and a call to action. It is imported by exactly one file: its own test suite.

What users actually meet is a bare line of unstyled text in search, repeated “No events or tasks” rows in Agenda, and blank cells everywhere else. Whatever the redesign specifies here has to be matched by actually rendering it.

05Constraints

What the build can absorb

Engineering realities, not preferences. Anything outside these is a conversation rather than a no.

Tokens first Deliver decisions as token values, or as a new token set with a stated mapping. Loose hex values that don't resolve to tokens won't survive implementation.
Stack Tailwind v4 and shadcn/ui stay. Radix primitives determine the DOM and accessibility semantics of every select, dialog, popover, dropdown, tooltip and checkbox — designs needing a different DOM for those need flagging.
Themes Light only today. Every colour is already a variable, so the architecture supports a dark theme; the values don't exist. Propose one and it needs the full second set.
Keyboard The full shortcut model is a requirement, not a nicety — search, create, view switching, period navigation, and keyboard drag for moving events.
Accessibility AA contrast, a visible focus state on every control, 44px coarse-pointer targets, errors carrying shape as well as colour, reduced-motion honoured, and a keyboard equivalent for every drag. This is the floor.
Motion 120–200ms, colour and transform only. No layout-shifting animation except the deliberate collapse when a task is ticked off.
Type Three families already load. Changing them is fine; a fourth needs justifying.
Data Fixed. Don't imply fields that don't exist — no attendees, attachments, video links or labels.
Recurrence Expanded server-side per query range, never materialised. Editing an instance in place has to account for the parent / exception / exclusion model.
06The ask

What we want back

  1. Token values — colour roles and tints, a type scale with line-heights and tracking, radii, shadows, motion, and a spacing scale, which currently doesn't exist in any form.
  2. One categorical palette for calendars and event colour overrides, replacing all three of the palettes in Finding One.
  3. Redesigned screens at 1440 and 390: month, week, day, agenda, task panel, event drawer, task drawer, search, settings, and the four auth screens.
  4. A mobile information architecture that answers Finding Two — specifically, where create, search, tasks and account live on a phone.
  5. Component specs across every state: rest, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, invalid. Focus, hover and invalid are currently global rules rather than per-component decisions, so they need deciding.
  6. Empty, loading, error and offline states for every screen you touch.
